chunks: Abdullah ibn al-Salt from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Takbir (saying Allahu Akbar) for the deceased, and he said, 'Five.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: A title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the sixth Imam.
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), a key component of the funeral prayer.
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: The deceased person for whom the funeral prayer is performed.

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirat are recited in the Shia funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi establishes the five Takbirat as the normative practice for the funeral prayer (Salat al-Mayyit), a ruling that distinguishes Shia jurisprudence from the four Takbirat commonly observed in Sunni traditions. The concise dialogue with Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) underscores the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in defining ritual specifics, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on following the Imams' precise instructions for acts of worship.
